claim: Google's AI content guidance (updated 2026-10-01) says it is critical to manually factcheck and review all AI-generated content for accuracy and trustworthiness before publishing.
sourceName: Google Search Central: Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website

claim: Google says this review also applies to metadata that can appear in Search results: <title> elements, meta description elements, structured data, and alternate text for images.
sourceName: Google Search Central: Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website

claim: Google says using generative AI tools to generate many pages without adding value for users may violate its spam policy on scaled content abuse.
sourceName: Google Search Central: Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website

claim: Google's guidance says Search Quality Rater ratings don't directly influence ranking; raters help evaluate the performance of its ranking systems.
sourceName: Google Search Central: Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website

claim: In a Feb 8, 2023 post, Google said its ranking systems reward original, high-quality content and that it focuses on the quality of content rather than how content is produced.
sourceName: Google Search Central Blog: Google Search's guidance about AI-generated content (Feb 8, 2023)

claim: Google's 2023 FAQ says appropriate use of AI or automation is not against its guidelines; using it to generate content primarily to manipulate rankings violates its spam policies.
sourceName: Google Search Central Blog: Google Search's guidance about AI-generated content (Feb 8, 2023)

claim: Google says using AI doesn't give content any special gains: "It's just content." If it is useful, helpful, original, and satisfies aspects of E-E-A-T, it might do well.
sourceName: Google Search Central Blog: Google Search's guidance about AI-generated content (Feb 8, 2023)

claim: Google defines scaled content abuse as many pages generated primarily to manipulate search rankings and not help users, typically unoriginal and low-value, no matter how it's created.
sourceName: Google Search Central: Spam policies for Google web search

claim: Google's spam policies list using generative AI tools or similar tools to generate many pages without adding value for users as an example of scaled content abuse.
sourceName: Google Search Central: Spam policies for Google web search

claim: Google announced the scaled content abuse policy on March 5, 2024, saying it applies whether content is produced through automation, human efforts, or a combination.
sourceName: Google Search Central Blog: March 2024 core update and new spam policies

claim: Google's Search Status Dashboard says the August 2026 spam update was released Aug 18, 2026, applies globally and to all languages, and finished rolling out Aug 21, 2026.
sourceName: Google Search Status Dashboard: August 2026 spam update

claim: Google didn't announce new spam policies or a companion blog post with the August 2026 spam update, according to Search Engine Journal.
Rater guidelines section 4.6.5 (Scaled Content Abuse) tells raters to rate such pages Lowest no matter how they are created, even if unsure whether generative AI tools were used.
sourceName: Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines (General Guidelines, September 11, 2025)

claim: Rater guidelines section 4.6.6 applies Lowest when almost all main content is copied, paraphrased, embedded, auto or AI generated, or reposted with little effort, originality, or value.
sourceName: Google Search Quality Rater Guidelines (General Guidelines, September 11, 2025)

claim: Google says AI or automation disclosures are useful where someone might think "How was this created?" and to consider adding them when it would be reasonably expected.
sourceName: Google Search Central: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content

claim: Google says Merchant Center requires AI-generated images to carry IPTC TrainedAlgorithmicMedia metadata, and AI-generated product titles and descriptions to be labeled as AI-generated.
sourceName: Google Search Central: Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website

claim: Google says it uses a variety of systems, including SpamBrain, that analyze patterns and signals to help identify spam content, however it is produced.
sourceName: Google Search Central Blog: Google Search's guidance about AI-generated content (Feb 8, 2023)

claim: Google's John Mueller said what matters is the overall quality published; using AI tools to get started is not a problem on its own, nor a sign content is automatically high quality.
sourceName: Google Search Central: June 2024 SEO Office Hours transcript
